seoTitle: How to Fix the Canonical Tag Error in Shopify
metaDescription: Resolve the 'alternate page with proper canonical tag' warning in Shopify by understanding canonical URLs and how search engines index them.
intro: Seeing an 'alternate page with proper canonical tag' notice in your site's indexing reports can be confusing if you're not familiar with how canonical URLs work. This guide explains what this Shopify notice generally means and the steps to check and clean up your canonical setup.

steps.heading: Understand what the notice means
steps.body: This status generally indicates a search engine found a page pointing to another URL as the canonical version, which is often expected behavior rather than a true error.

steps.heading: Check your product and collection URLs
steps.body: Review pages that may exist in multiple variations, such as with different URL parameters, to see how their canonical tags are set.

steps.heading: Confirm Shopify's default canonical tags
steps.body: Shopify automatically adds canonical tags to most pages, so verify these are pointing to the correct primary URL for each page.

steps.heading: Review theme customizations
steps.body: If your theme has been customized, check that no code changes have accidentally altered or removed canonical tags.

steps.heading: Monitor your indexing reports
steps.body: After reviewing your setup, keep an eye on your search console reports to see if the notice clears over time.

faq.question: Is the canonical tag notice always a problem?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — it often just reflects that a duplicate or variant URL correctly points to another page as its canonical version.

faq.question: Does Shopify set canonical tags automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, Shopify includes canonical tags by default on most pages, which usually handles common duplicate content situations.

faq.question: Can theme customization cause canonical tag issues?
faq.answer: Yes, custom code changes to your theme can sometimes interfere with or override the default canonical tags Shopify sets.

faq.question: Will this affect my store's search rankings?
faq.answer: In most cases this notice is informational rather than a ranking penalty, but persistent duplicate content issues are still worth reviewing.
